record.name: Israel
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. Government sources describe the National AI Directorate and an institute for applied AI, alongside cyber defence and regulatory testing. The AI Index reports an AI Security Research Unit, unconfirmed by primary sources.

partial.scope: Negative-status confidence, preserved query provenance, national/official-language search coverage and source-independence audit; this is not a full recheck of all record fields.

Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. No retained English query. The retrieved material does not sufficiently establish the national AI governance arrangements. No new search or full recheck.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.

English searches for a national AI safety, security or evaluation institute, commitment, proposal or study. English searches surfaced a conflicting secondary claim in Stanford's 2026 AI Index: Israel is listed with an operational 'AI Security Research Unit' (printed p.165), citing All Tech Is Human's 2025 landscape article. Bounded exact-name searches did not retrieve primary government confirmation, and the cited catalogue's country classifications require caution. The Knesset national-programme result concerns governance and investment; opening it returned a geographic-access block. Retain low-confidence ambiguity pending primary verification; do not infer an established institute from the catalogue. Partial check only; the last full-check date is unchanged.
Hebrew and English status review of the reported security unit and national AI programme; no full recheck of unrelated fields.

Retained low confidence for the unverified third-party claim about an AI Security Research Unit, distinguishing the evidence gap from classification disagreement. Partial check; the last full-check date is unchanged.

Aligned current rationale wording with the consolidated capability-or-behaviour-risk test, removing the old severity requirement. This editorial consistency pass adds no research claim and does not change status or the last full-check date.

Re-ran searches in English and Hebrew for a government-designated institute that evaluates advanced models, or a commitment, proposal or study naming one. No qualifying institute or commitment was identified, and nothing new on the reported AI Security Research Unit was found. Kept low: the earlier unresolved evidence gap on that unit remains. Partial check; the last full-check date is unchanged.

News search from 17 October 2026 in English and Hebrew, with the innovation, science and technology ministry's Hebrew news listing (newest 3 November). No qualifying item was found. Infrastructure plans and independent think-tank work do not establish the government AI Security Research Unit in the record, and that evidence gap remains. The English-language listings were out of date and were not used. Partial check, not a full record re-check.

check.language_note: The recorded he queries use a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. English queries were also run on 17 October 2026; the earlier round did not extend national or official-language coverage. The additional status review used Hebrew and English searches and retrieved primary material in both languages. Arabic coverage was not extended. Search batches for the additional status review, using 1-based positions in check.searches: 4, 5, 6, 7; 8; 9. Each group records the same exact registered URLs found in its combined search results, without attribution to an individual query. Explicit page opens and finds and unverified URL variants are excluded. Groups list the recorded queries; some requests also contained additional queries retained in the research evidence. On 24 October 2026 the record was searched again in English and Hebrew; the result links of each query were matched against registered sources in the same way.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: The regional Arcadia abstract does not supply a retrieved country-specific institutional excerpt independently corroborating the national directorate account. Confidence was low under that rule; none_identified is a bounded search finding, not proof of absence.
check.governance_note: Retrieved government programme material identifies the Directorate, applied research institute, regulatory testing and AI cyber-defence work. The Hebrew Nagel report concerns national AI research, compute and coordination. The only evidence for the separately reported AI Security Research Unit is a third-party catalogue entry that supplies no primary citation for the unit; its existence and remit have not been verified in a primary source. This evidence gap keeps confidence low.

related_bodies.name: National AI Directorate
related_bodies.role: It coordinates the national AI programme, including compute, research, skills and applications, as a Prime Minister's Office body. Its programme page does not identify a qualifying institute to evaluate the safety of advanced models.

related_bodies.name: National Institute for Impact Driven AI
related_bodies.role: It is described in the National AI Directorate's programme as applying AI to medicine, genomics, climate and infrastructure. No explicit mandate to evaluate advanced models for capabilities or behaviour risks was identified.

record.notes:
The cabinet approved the national AI programme in June 2026; the Directorate's plan lists a national AI institute, dedicated cybersecurity laboratories and a national ethics council, whose retrieved descriptions do not establish evaluation of advanced models for capabilities or behaviour risks.

The National AI Directorate's programme page and Foreign Ministry account were retrieved in English, with Hebrew evidence from the Nagel committee report. The programme describes an institute for applied AI and regulatory testing, plus separate defence of AI infrastructure and systems; these do not state a mandate to evaluate advanced models for capabilities or behaviour risks. The All Tech Is Human table cited by AI Index was retrieved and visually checked. It attributes an AI Security Research Unit to the National Cyber Directorate, but gives no primary citation for that row. Hebrew and English follow-up searches did not verify it. The Directorate's August 2026 plan provides for three laboratories with the National Cyber Directorate, one of them to secure AI systems against attack, which does not meet the definition; the plan names no AI security research unit. The two catalogues therefore remain one unresolved evidence chain.

next_check.reason: Verify the reported National Cyber Directorate AI Security Research Unit through a primary act; none was found in October 2026. Check whether the planned laboratories with the National Cyber Directorate are created and whether any receives a remit to evaluate advanced models for capabilities or behaviour risks.
